title: Best Car Battery Chargers UK
short: Six car battery chargers tested on flat and heavily discharged batteries, timing how fast each reached 80% charge and checking safety features.
intro: A dead car battery is one of the most common reasons for a failed MOT or a no-start on a cold morning, and a decent charger can keep an occasionally-used car's battery topped up between drives. This guide is based on Auto Express's tested roundup, where testers charged three 12V batteries with each unit: a 68Ah battery discharged to 10.5V (timing how long it took to reach 80% charge), a heavily discharged 95Ah pack, and a deeply flat 5Ah battery at 2V, alongside checking instruction clarity, cable length, waterproofing and safety features.

products.name: 12V Intelligent Charger
products.best_for: Buyers who want quick, reliable charging with essential features at the lowest price on test
products.key_spec: 10A output, 3m total cable reach, IP65 rated, LCD display
products.summary: Auto Express's overall winner, combining the essential features most drivers need with quick charging, a rugged IP65-rated design, and the lowest price of the group, earning a full 5-star rating. Testers found the LCD display clear and the 3m combined cable reach practical for most engine bay layouts.
pros: Lowest price of the group tested
cons: Cable reach shorter than the Ring and NOCO

products.name: Ultra Charge 10
products.best_for: Buyers who want the fastest charge and don't mind paying more for extra features
products.key_spec: 10A output, 4.3m cable, colour LCD, alternator-test function, carrying case
products.summary: Auto Express found this was the fastest of the group to reach 80% charge, backed by a colour LCD screen, a handy alternator-test function and a carrying case for storage. Testers felt the extra £28 over the Draper isn't fully justified by the performance gain, but it's a strong choice if you want the quickest results and the added features.
cons: Costs more without a proportionate performance gain

products.name: Genius5
products.best_for: Buyers who want a neat, wall-mountable charger for permanent garage storage
products.key_spec: 5A output, 4m cable, Velcro-strapped wall mount, Force Charge mode
products.summary: Auto Express liked this charger's elegant simplicity, and it's the only one on test with a Velcro-strapped wall mount for tidy garage storage. A four-metre cable, large battery clamps and a Force Charge mode for severely flat batteries all impressed, though its 5A maximum output means it isn't the fastest charger here.
pros: Force Charge mode for severely flat batteries
cons: Lower 5A maximum output means slower charging

products.name: 5 Select
products.best_for: Owners of classic or older vehicles running 6V electrical systems
products.summary: Auto Express notes this targets classic car owners specifically, with a switchable 6V/12V setting that most modern chargers don't offer. It's limited to lead-acid batteries only and its 3A output was the slowest on test, but for older vehicles needing 6V charging it fills a gap the rest of the group can't.

products.name: NXT 5
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise spark-free operation above all else
products.key_spec: Spark-free connection, matches rivals' core specs, premium price
products.summary: Auto Express highlighted this charger's spark-free operation as a genuine safety advantage over the rest of the group, useful when connecting clamps near a battery that may be venting gas. Otherwise it matches its rivals' core specs, but carries the highest price on test.

specs.Output: Comparable to other 12V chargers on test

pros: Matches rivals on core charging ability
cons: No standout performance advantage to match the price

products.name: Car Battery Charger
products.best_for: Nobody — Auto Express found it failed on safety
products.key_spec: Budget unbranded charger, failed safety tests in testing
products.summary: Auto Express included this as a budget benchmark and found its low price undermined by an unreadable display, impractically short cables, and outright failed safety tests. It's included here as a warning rather than a recommendation: the cheapest option on test was also the only one testers flagged as unsafe.

guide.q: What amperage charger do I need?
guide.a: Auto Express found a 10A charger like the Draper or Ring reaches 80% charge fastest, suiting a car driven daily where you need it back quickly. A lower 5A charger like the NOCO Genius5 is gentler and fine for a car that's only occasionally off the road, or for trickle-charging over winter.

guide.q: Do I need a smart or intelligent charger?
guide.a: All the chargers Auto Express recommends here are 'intelligent', meaning they automatically adjust charging rate and stop at full charge, so they're safe to leave connected for extended periods without overcharging the battery. The Temu charger's failed safety tests are a reminder that not every budget unit can be trusted to do this reliably.

Only if you own a classic car with an original 6V electrical system. Auto Express notes the OptiMate 5 Select is the only charger on test with a switchable 6V/12V setting for this purpose; modern cars all use 12V so this won't matter for most drivers.

Auto Express highlighted the CTEK NXT 5's spark-free operation as a genuine safety feature, reducing risk when connecting clamps to a battery that may be venting hydrogen gas, particularly relevant for older or heavily discharged batteries.
